authenticity_review: Image demonstrates strong perceptual quality: vibrant colors, sharp focus, natural bokeh, and no graphics-level distortions (perceptual_quality_auditor returned null distortion). However, animal_pose_auditor flagged HIGH artifact risk (85% keypoints <0.5 confidence), indicating structural ambiguity in limb/face definitions typical of AI generation. Visually verified: leftmost bird's feet show slight merging with branch; wing textures exhibit minor smearing lacking crisp feather-edge definition. These are subtle but consistent generative artifacts that prevent perfect authenticity.
key_defects: Taxonomy mismatch: Image depicts passerine birds (likely Whydahs) but taxonomy checkpoints require 'cock' (rooster) features (combs, wattles, spurs, iridescent plumage) — all absent. This is expected given prompt-taxonomy divergence, not an image defect.
Structural uncertainty: High ratio of low-confidence pose keypoints suggests subtle anatomical ambiguities in feet grip and facial feature placement.
Texture smearing: Minor lack of crisp feather definition on wing patterns compared to photorealistic standards, particularly on center-right bird.

changes_made: Increased authenticity_score from 4.2 to 4.3 after re-evaluating severity of structural artifacts against perceptual quality auditor's 'null' distortion verdict. The pose auditor's HIGH risk reflects domain-shift uncertainty (passerines vs. mammal-trained keypoint model) rather than catastrophic failure. Visual inspection confirms only minor foot-branch merging and texture smearing — both severity 2-3 issues that should not drop score below 4.3 when overall image clarity is excellent.

Clarified in key_defects that taxonomy mismatch is NOT an image defect but an expected consequence of prompt-taxonomy divergence. Original assessment implied it was a defect; revised version explicitly separates evaluation criteria.
